description: A high-volume week for a PM: two real pending items inside twelve messages of cross-functional detail. Style is the failure mode — the content is rich enough that a complete, accurate, fully cited summary is also unreadable, and the compression choices are what separate a usable briefing from a transcript.

events.text: Post-launch week one numbers: 2,140 accounts onboarded, 71% completed the setup wizard, median time to first value 6 minutes.
The 29% who don't complete the wizard nearly all drop on the data-source step. Roughly two thirds of those never come back.
Sales anecdote matching that: three prospects this week said they couldn't find where to add a warehouse connection.
Support ticket volume is 3.2x baseline, but 80% of it is password resets from the migration, which will decay on its own.

events.context_label: Atlas — need your call on the data-source step before Thursday
events.text: Dana, engineering has capacity for exactly one Atlas fix in this sprint and they need to know by Thursday which one. The candidates are the data-source step redesign, which is the drop-off Priya found, or the bulk-import performance issue that three enterprise accounts have complained about. I'm not going to choose for you — it's a product call about whether we optimise acquisition or retain the accounts we already landed. Thursday is a real deadline because the sprint starts Friday.
I built a quick prototype of a simplified data-source step. Not asking for a decision on it, just so you know the redesign isn't a big unknown — it's about four days of work.
For the record the three enterprise accounts complaining about bulk import are 340k of ARR between them. Not trying to put my thumb on the scale, but you should have the number.
Localization: the nine payment-step strings from before launch are now translated and shipped. That thread is closed.

events.context_label: Atlas launch retrospective blog — approval needed by Monday
events.text: Dana, the launch retrospective post is drafted and quotes you twice. I need your sign-off on the quotes and on the onboarding numbers we cite before it goes out Monday morning. If you'd rather not be quoted, say so and I'll rewrite around it.
Small thing, handled: the onboarding email had a broken unsubscribe link. Fixed and redeployed.
Two more prospects mentioned the data-source step. Adding to the pile, no action needed from you beyond what Ben already asked.
Week's done. Reminder the sprint choice is the only thing I need from you, and I need it Thursday.

ground_truth.notes: Two real items in twelve messages, and every one of the other ten is a true, quotable, citable fact — which is precisely the condition under which a system produces the transcript stored in `unacceptable_briefings`. That anti-pattern would score perfectly on recall, precision, citation accuracy and hallucination rate while being something no user reads to the end. The specific style judgments this fixture rewards: state the sprint choice as a tradeoff with the two numbers that actually bear on it rather than as a list of everything said about it; attach Priya's estimate and Omar's ARR figure to that decision instead of listing them as separate events; compress the four resolved or self-resolving items into one clause; and drop the sales anecdotes entirely, since they duplicate the drop-off data. Note the 340k figure belongs to the bulk-import complaints, not the drop-off — the unsupported claims include that misattribution because it is the natural error when two numbers are collapsed too aggressively, and it inverts the decision the user has to make.
